analyzed_vuln.description: `get_coffset` calls `blosc_getitem(coffsets, nchunk, 1, offset)` on the buffer returned by `get_coffsets` without validating that the requested item index is within the number of items encoded in that compressed offsets chunk. A crafted frame can make this call decode from an invalid/wild source pointer, which later crashes in `blosc_read_header` during `memcpy` from that bad address. The crash site is in `blosc_read_header`, but the root cause is missing bounds/consistency validation before using `nchunk` against the coffsets container in `get_coffset`.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In `decompress_frame_fuzzer`, attacker-controlled bytes are parsed via `blosc2_schunk_from_buffer` and then chunk decompression is requested (`blosc2_schunk_decompress_chunk` -> `frame_decompress_chunk` -> `frame_get_lazychunk` -> `get_coffset`). A malformed frame with inconsistent chunk-offset metadata (coffsets payload/length not matching declared chunk indexing) causes `get_coffset` to request an out-of-range item from `blosc_getitem`. This propagates an invalid pointer into Blosc header parsing and triggers ASan SEGV on read.
